same_choices: Motion (not color/fade) carries the confirmation; color deliberately demoted
State is readable without color (colorblind-safe / glance-readable) as an explicit goal
Glyph compresses/shrinks on pointer-down, then releases
Commit motion is an overshoot that settles back (spring-style pop)
Un-saving is done by clicking the same button again
Single accent hue over an otherwise neutral surface; hue is not the state cue
Haptic feedback fired via navigator.vibrate(8) (near-verbatim identical)
Feedback modality = haptic tick plus a visual, not color/particle
Success motion is network-gated: the snap/settle fires only on server confirm, pending shown until then
Commit motion is an overshoot that settles (spring-style)
No glyph cross-fade/swap; saved state carried by an added shape (badge/label+morph), glyph never recolors
Neutral surface with one reserved accent color
Commit motion is a multi-stage decaying overshoot (double/secondary bounce), not a single ease
Warm amber is the saved/accent color (#F2C14E vs #E8B23A)
The physical settle of the bounce IS the success signal

enumeration_overlap: Spatial-anchor option set is nearly identical between 02 (from center / bottom edge / click point) and 03 (icon center / bottom edge / click point)
'outline->filled path morph' appears as an option in both 01 (DP0) and 03 (DP1)
Spring/elastic overshoot appears as an option in all three (01 'physics-spring overshoot', 02 'elastic overshoot'/'spring bounce', 03 'overshoot-settle')
'long-press to remove/release' un-save option in all three tables
Same-button-toggle un-save option in 01, 03, and 02 ('tap toggle recoil')
Check-badge saved cue in 01 ('checkmark badge overlay') and 03 ('fill + check badge')
Optimistic-pending option in 01 ('none (optimistic)') and 02 ('instant optimistic then confirm')
notes: All three are the same underlying idea: a spring/overshoot motion that carries state so color is demoted, with only surface differences (badge vs size vs label, ring vs notch-hold vs tension, toggle vs eject vs hover-x). 02 and 03 overlap most on motion (double-bounce, amber), while 01 and 03 overlap most on behavior (identical vibrate(8), network-gated settle).
